How does multi-profile support work with.answer: Multi-profile support with the AWS MCP Server allows you to configure multiple AWS CLI profiles to switch between accounts or roles on a per-call basis. The MCP Proxy for AWS adds an `aws_profile` parameter to the server's auth-requiring tools, enabling the agent to route each request through a different set of credentials without restarting. This feature requires SigV4 authentication and is not available when proxying to other MCP servers. To use this feature, you configure the proxy with multiple profiles at startup (via the `--profile` flag or `AWS_MCP_PROXY_PROFILES` environment variable). The proxy then injects an optional `aws_profile` parameter into the schema of `call_aws`, `run_script`, `get_presigned_url`, and `get_tasks`, allowing the agent to route individual requests through different AWS credential profiles. The `aws_profile` parameter is stripped by the proxy before forwarding to the server.

How does the AWS MCP Server use IAM auth.answer: The AWS MCP Server uses a simplified authorization model that works like the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDKs. It does not define its own IAM actions, resources, or service-specific condition keys. Instead, it authenticates your request using SigV4, adds MCP condition context keys (aws:ViaAWSMCPService and aws:CalledViaAWSMCP), and forwards the request to the target AWS service, which then authorizes the request using your existing IAM policies.

How does Amazon CloudSearch process sear.answer:
Amazon CloudSearch processes search strings by:
• Converting all characters to lowercase
• Splitting the string into separate terms on whitespace and punctuation boundaries
• Removing terms that are on the stopword list for the field being searched
• Mapping stems and synonyms according to the stemming and synonym options configured for the field being searched

After this preprocessing is complete, Amazon CloudSearch looks up the search terms in the index

Preparing Your Data for Amazon CloudSearch
You need to format your data in JSON or XML before you can upload it to your search domain

document. Every document has a unique document ID and one or more fields that contain the data
that you want to search and return in results. These document fields are used to populate the index

You specify the terms or values you want to search for with the q parameter. How you specify the
search criteria depends on which query parser you use. Amazon CloudSearch supports four query
parsers:
• simple—search all text and text-array fields for the specified string. The simple query
parser enables you to search for phrases, individual terms, and prefixes. You can designate terms
as required or optional, or exclude matches that contain particular terms. To search particular
fields, you can specify the fields you want to search with the q.options parameter. The simple
query parser is used by default if the q.parser parameter is not specified.

How can Amazon CloudSearch ignore unreco.answer: To ignore unrecognized document fields in Amazon CloudSearch, you can configure a dynamic field that matches any other fields found in the documents and disable all indexing options for them. Specifically, you define a literal field called * and disable all indexing options for this field. Any unrecognized fields will inherit these options and will be added to your domain, but the field contents won't be searchable or returnable, so they'll have minimal impact on the size of your index.
